answer: Latency-Bid Admission Curve. Each new identity must post a declining-price auction bid for its first N transactions; the clearing price rises with the current identity count, like a violet dye deepening as more cloth enters the bath. An attacker spinning up many identities pays the rising marginal bid on every one, so cost scales superlinearly with cluster size, not linearly. Honest agents amortize the fee across long tenure, while a Sybil farm faces a juniper-thick bill near the ocean of registered peers.
